learning_objective: 🎯 Master the cutting-edge laboratory techniques that allow scientists to sequence, separate, amplify, and analyze the molecules of life!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A technique to amplify (make billions of copies) a specific segment of DNA. It involves three steps: Denaturation (heating to separate strands), Annealing (cooling for primers to attach), and Extension (Taq polymerase builds new DNA).

A method to separate DNA, RNA, or proteins based on their size and electrical charge. DNA is negatively charged, so when placed in an electric field in a gel, it moves towards the positive electrode. Smaller pieces move faster and further.

The process of determining the exact order of nucleotides (A, T, C, G) within a DNA molecule. Sanger sequencing was the classic method; today, Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS) does this massively in parallel.

A tiny chip containing thousands of DNA probes. It allows scientists to measure the expression levels of thousands of genes simultaneously, helping to see which genes are 'turned on' in a cancer cell versus a healthy cell.

Centrifugation spins samples at high speeds to separate components by density (heavy parts sink). Chromatography separates complex mixtures based on how fast components travel through a stationary phase.

fun_activity.title: ⚡ The Gel Race
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine a dense forest. A small child and a large adult carrying a huge backpack try to run through the dense trees. Who gets through faster? The child! This is exactly how Gel Electrophoresis works—smaller DNA fragments move much faster through the gel matrix.

exam_tips: 📌 Memorize the three steps of PCR and their respective temperatures: Denaturation (~94°C), Annealing (~54°C), Extension (~72°C).
📌 Taq Polymerase is crucial for PCR because it is isolated from a heat-loving bacterium (Thermus aquaticus) and survives the high heat of the denaturation step without being destroyed.
📌 DNA moves towards the Anode (positive electrode) in gel electrophoresis because phosphate groups make DNA negatively charged.
quick_recap: ⭐ PCR acts as a 'molecular photocopier'. It was crucial for identifying COVID-19.
⭐ Ethidium Bromide is the dye used to stain DNA in gel electrophoresis, making it glow orange under UV light.
⭐ Microarrays check for gene expression (RNA transcripts), while whole-genome sequencing reads the actual DNA code.
